The fast food chain revealed the partnership on November 19, confirming that the holiday menu will launch at participating US locations on December 1, 2026. The promotion includes new food items, collectible packaging, and special merchandise for both adults and children.

The collaboration comes as Peanuts celebrates more than 75 years since its debut in 1950, with Burger King introducing two different meal options inspired by the franchise’s characters.

The main offering is the Peanuts Pack, which comes inside a collectible Snoopy Doghouse Box and includes one of two exclusive Snoopy holiday beanies.

Customers can choose between a Whopper with Cheese or 10-piece Chicken Nuggets, with the latter served alongside a upcoming Woodstock Golden Ranch dipping sauce.

The meal also introduces Charlie Brown Loaded Potato Tots, featuring crispy, coin-shaped potatoes filled with cheese, bacon bits, sour cream, and chives.

Each Peanuts Pack comes with one of two collectible Snoopy beanies. One features a brown knit design with Snoopy resting on his red doghouse, while the other is red and depicts Snoopy wearing a Santa hat.

Burger King is also introducing a Peanuts-inspired King Jr. Meal, which includes a hamburger, cheeseburger, or four-piece Chicken Nuggets, alongside a choice of fries or applesauce and milk or apple juice.

Each kids’ meal comes in its own Snoopy Doghouse Box and includes one of eight collectible Peanuts toys.

Burger King releases Hello Kitty kids meals with rare golden collectible toys.

Burger King unveils bizarre new burger with popcorn as a topping.

Burger King is releasing a Chocolate Whopper packed with dessert toppings.

The collection features Charlie Brown, Lucy, Linus, Sally, three different holiday-themed Snoopy figures, and a Snoopy Doghouse that comes with stickers for customization.

“Peanuts has been part of holiday family traditions for generations, and we can’t wait to bring Snoopy and the gang to Burger King this holiday season!” stated Joel Yashinsky, Chief Marketing Officer of Burger King US and Canada.

“At BK, we go all out on partnerships to create fun experiences for everyone – with newly introduced menu items, creative packaging and crowns, collectible Snoopy beanies and Peanuts toys and more, we’ve created something really special. It’s holiday fun for all, and we can’t wait to welcome families and fans to BK to celebrate throughout the month of December!”.

Both meals will be available beginning December 1 at participating Burger King restaurants across the US, through the tech giant’s website, and via its mobile app while supplies last.

Burger King has not revealed pricing for either meal or specified when the promotion will end.

The Peanuts collaboration isn’t the only holiday-themed fast food promotion arriving in December.

McDonald’s has also announced a limited-time Home Alone Meal launching December 1, featuring Little Nero’s Pizza McShaker Fries and collectible socks inspired by the holiday movie. The promotion also brings Macaulay Culkin back as Kevin McCallister as part of the chain’s seasonal campaign.

On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars.
  • The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN.
  • MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars.

The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago.

MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars. The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result.

Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface, and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place.

NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind, as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time.

Recent findings suggest that after its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014. The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind.

"The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come.".

In a recent development, MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study.

According to recent reports, NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent, with NASA losing communication with the orbiter.

An investigation later found that the probe sent its final signal on Dec. 6, 2025 as it was heading behind Mars (as seen from Earth). But when it emerged on the other side, it had gone into an uncontrollable spin that led to a loss of power, dooming the spacecraft.

NASA tried in vain to recover the spacecraft over several months, ultimately declaring the mission over in June 2026.

"Best. Mars. Mission. Ever," Shannon Curry, MAVEN's principal investigator, said of the probe's entire 12.5-year mission when it ended. The team "really experienced the loss of a loved one with the end of the mission here.".

📅 23 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1307 w)

Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist

📅 23 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1307 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A newly introduced optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles.
  • Sources indicate that researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a latest type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost.
  • Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A newly introduced optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.

Sources indicate that researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a latest type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.

Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.

Industry observers note that the researchers believe their upcoming design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.

A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision.

Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The latest device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.

To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.

"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," noted Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system.".

The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.

Another vital advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.

A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare.

It has been revealed that to evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.

It has been revealed that when used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.

The healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.

Industry observers note that the researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.

"These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," stated Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment.".

The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.

Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough.

Sources indicate that the newly introduced spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.

Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.

In a recent development, the Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.

"This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," stated Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible.".

Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.

Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices.

The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.

In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is at the moment practical.

In a recent development, healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.

"Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work highlights that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day.".

As photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that despite its somewhat muted critical reception, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 has predictably topped the US video game charts in October. The Infinity Ward-developed shooter was October's best-selling game in the US across digital and retail, beating the month's other significant-hitters, including Gears of War: E-Day and Star Wars: Galactic Racer.

That's according to market analysis firm Circana's latest US market report, which revealed Modern Warfare 4 was October's leader in dollar sales. This marks the 19th-year running that a Call of Duty game topped the charts in its release month, a streak that began with November 2008's COD: World at War.

However, despite a successful October, Modern Warfare 4 hasn't managed to land in Circana's top ten list of year-to-date biggest sellers. In fact, the only COD title on the list is the Black Ops 2 port released this summer. NBA 2K27 continues to lead Circana's ranking, having overtaken Resident Evil: Requiem last month to secure the top spot. It's a reverse of Circana's September report, when NBA 2K27 failed to lead its own debut month but claimed the top spot in the year-to-date list. Here's the list of the top 10 year-to-date:.

Away from Modern Warfare 4, October saw the release of several other well-performing and critically acclaimed games, and six of the top ten were upcoming releases. That hasn't stopped Circana from posting 14 percent lower spending on games compared to October last year. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted much of that dip can be attributed to a big slump in mobile spending, and also because October 2025 was particularly strong, with both Battlefield 6 and Pokémon Legends: Z-A releasing. Here's October's top 10:.

In Eurogamer's Modern Warfare 4 review, Dom Peppiatt awarded it four stars, writing: "Modern Warfare 4 represents the highest tide for Call of Duty in seven years. Infinity Ward needed to pull off a balancing act I don't envy; injecting just enough nostalgia into a series propped up with so many conventions and expectations there's barely room for anything fresh, alongside enough innovation and intrigue to keep people interested.".

GPS services, a bright, always-on display, and continuous health sensors like SpO2 can squeeze the most juice out of your smartwatch.

Wear OS software is used by many of the most popular smartwatch brands, including Google, Samsung, and OnePlus. Both the Google Pixel Watch and Samsung Galaxy Watch’s largest batteries last approximately 40 hours. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • Today's best RAM will look huge compared to upcoming DDR6 memory.
  • JEDEC's DDR6 preview highlights improvements in various areas, including performance, capacity, reliability, and power efficiency.
  • One of the most notable differences is that DDR6 memory modules will measure just 74mm in length, 44% shorter than DDR5’s 133mm memory modules.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Today's best RAM will look huge compared to upcoming DDR6 memory. JEDEC has just released a preview of the DDR6 specification, confirming that next-generation memory modules will be 44% shorter than DDR5. That is only the physical aspect, though. From a performance perspective, DDR6 will debut at 12.8 GT/s, more than double DDR5's baseline transfer rate, while also quadrupling the memory bandwidth per memory module thanks to a new design.

JEDEC's DDR6 preview highlights improvements in various areas, including performance, capacity, reliability, and power efficiency. These advancements align with the upgrades DDR5 brought to the table when it introduced.

One of the most notable differences is that DDR6 memory modules will measure just 74mm in length, 44% shorter than DDR5’s 133mm memory modules. This makes DDR6 only 6% longer than DDR5 SO-DIMM modules, which you commonly find in laptops and mini-PCs.

Recent findings suggest that JEDEC has maintained the pin count for many years, sticking to 288 pins for DDR4 and DDR5. However, DDR6 may finally break that mould. Given the substantial reduction in length with DDR6 and the data bus width upgrade, it is reasonable to assume that DDR6 will have a completely different pinout and density. Sadly, JEDEC has not revealed the pin count for DDR6.

Early rumors suggested that DDR6 may be limited to CAMM form factors to feed the AI boom. However, JEDEC's announcement at least does not rule out other form factors. It appears JEDEC is still determining which form factors DDR6 will use. Potential options include RDIMM, UDIMM, and CAMM formats, just like DDR5.

Baseline JEDEC Bandwidth Per Module (GB/s).

Peak JEDEC Transfer Rates (MT/s).

Peak Baseline Bandwidth Per Module (GB/s).

According to recent reports, notably, JEDEC has increased the data bus width in DDR6 to 96 bits, a 50% boost over DDR5's 64 bits. The channel architecture for DDR6 will also change substantially. While DDR4 and DDR5 leveraged a single 64-bit channel and two 32-bit sub-channels, DDR6 takes a different approach. JEDEC will implement a design with four 24-bit sub-channels.

Using the baseline for comparison, DDR6 offers up to 153.6 GB/s of total module bandwidth, compared to DDR5's 38.4 GB/s. That is a 4X uplift in bandwidth. If we compare DDR5-9200 RDIMMs, which max out at 73.6 GB/s per module, with DDR6-12800 RDIMMs, the uplift is a little more than double.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

At least on the server side, DDR6 RDIMMs will start at DDR6-12800, whereas DDR5 RDIMMs topped out at DDR5-9200. JEDEC anticipates DDR6 reaching DDR6-14400 and beyond. This is for the server and enterprise market, though. It remains to be seen which DDR6 speed will launch in the consumer market. DDR5 commenced at DDR5-4800.

According to recent reports, DDR6 may be shorter than DDR5, but it makes up for it by having 2X the bank count. This will help push higher data rates and capacities. DDR6 will support 128Gb (16GB) dies, which represents a massive leap. We are looking at 4X the density of early DDR5 memory modules. Instead of placing chips side by side on the PCB, DDR6 enables die stacking, allowing manufacturers to place multiple dies on top of each other via Through-Silicon Vias (TSVs).

Consumer DDR5 memory modules right now sit at 64GB per module, while server RDIMMs have reached 512GB. DDR6 could raise module capacity to 128GB or 256GB and potentially scale RDIMMs to 1TB or more per slot.

Industry observers note that DDR6 has no official launch date. Many believe 2029 is a realistic target for commercialization. However, in the current state of things, it would be a miracle if DDR6 had no setbacks.

There's right now no timeline for a verdict, however, with one commentator suggesting a judgement could take weeks or months to arrive.

In a recent development, the case, which began in September and has included evidence from 23 claimants in the months since, must now be considered by the judge, who will determine if Rockstar unfairly dismissed employees in breach of their employment rights. Rockstar has been accused of unlawfully firing workers for being part of a union, but the GTA developer insists employees were dismissed for breaching confidentiality agreements.

People Makes Games' Chris Bratt has been following the case closely and reporting on proceedings as they've unfolded. With closing statements now complete, Bratt quoted Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying, "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as promptly as I possibly can.".

However, Bratt suggests it could be ""anywhere from a few weeks up to a few months before we actually hear the judgement", noting "The firings themselves, let's not forget, happened over a year ago now. This has been a slog.".

One fired Rockstar worker involved in the case spoke with Bratt after the closing statements to share their thoughts. "Honestly it's just sort of blended together," they remarked. "It’s been so long, that after the first six months or so it became the upcoming depressing reality. I'm hoping the judgement will release us from it.".

Last month, the conclusion of the tribunal hearing was delayed after cross examination of witnesses ran long.

Yesterday's closing statements come at a time when all eyes are on GTA 6 as it finally releases this week, concluding years of development for both current and former employees. Many of those workers involved in the case urged players to support the game despite the legal dispute.

Additionally, Rockstar employees are currently voting on whether they want recognised union representation at the studio. If the vote passes, it would be the largest recognised union across the entirety of the UK video game industry. The deadline for union votes is 26th November.

The promotion is intended to recreate the experience of opening a physical game case and finding a disc inside, something that has become less common as publishers increasingly move toward digital distribution.

According to KFC Spain, the initiative was created in response to the ongoing shift away from physical media, particularly as collectors and players continue to debate the future of boxed video games.

Industry News: Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (979 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips.
  • Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made crucial progress toward solving this problem.
  • Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This demonstrates that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an vital step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips. However, researchers have faced a significant challenge. When multiple silicon qubits are controlled at the same time, their operations tend to become less accurate. Building practical, large quantum computers will require scientists to control many qubits simultaneously while keeping errors to a minimum.

Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made crucial progress toward solving this problem. In a study published in Nature Physics, the team demonstrated highly accurate control of several silicon spin qubits operating simultaneously. Their experiments used an array of five qubits connected to a shared microwave control line. By identifying a major cause of errors during simultaneous operation, the scientists developed a technique to reduce those errors and maintain precision.

Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This demonstrates that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an vital step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors.".

Scientists Identify a Hidden Source of Quantum Computing Errors.

According to recent reports, unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, that can exist in combinations of both states. Silicon spin qubits store this information using the spin of individual electrons confined within silicon. Performing reliable quantum calculations requires extremely precise control over these electron spins.

In a recent development, microwave signals provide that control, but operating multiple qubits simultaneously can create unwanted effects that interfere with their accuracy. The researchers traced much of this problem to a phenomenon called the AC Stark shift.

This effect occurs when microwave control signals alter a qubit's effective energy levels, producing changes in the phase of its quantum state. Those phase shifts can disrupt the intended operation of individual qubits, particularly when several are being controlled at once.

To counteract the problem, the team created a calibration method that compensates for these unwanted shifts. Rather than separately calibrating every possible combination of qubits, the technique relies on calibrations performed between pairs of qubits. This makes the approach more practical for systems containing larger numbers of quantum bits.

"Rather than requiring an entirely separate calibration procedure for every possible combination of qubits, our method uses calibrations between pairs of qubits to compensate for the unwanted phase shifts," explains Yi-Hsien Wu, the first author who carried out the experiments as part of his PhD research.

Quantum Qubits Achieve Accuracy Above 99.99%.

The researchers combined their calibration technique with an improved device design and carefully adjusted microwave control pulses. Their results highlighted that exceptionally high accuracy could be maintained even when multiple qubits were operating simultaneously.

When the five qubits were tested individually, each achieved single-qubit gate fidelity well above 99.99%, with the highest approaching 99.999%. Fidelity describes how closely a quantum operation matches its intended result.

The team then tested how well the system performed when several qubits were active together. With as many as three qubits operating simultaneously, fidelity remained above 99.99%. Even when all five qubits were controlled at once, accuracy stayed at approximately 99.9%, approaching the levels needed for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.

In a recent development, although the calibration method greatly reduced errors, it did not eliminate them entirely. The researchers found that the remaining loss of accuracy was linked to drive-induced decoherence, an effect caused by the greater microwave power required to operate multiple qubits simultaneously.

Unlike the unwanted phase shifts corrected by the latest technique, decoherence involves the loss of the delicate quantum coherence needed for reliable operations.

According to Camenzind, "This is a limitation, but further improvements to device design could help mitigate this source of error.".

A New Path Toward Larger Quantum Processors.

The findings show that controlling several silicon spin qubits at the same time does not necessarily require a major sacrifice in accuracy. By correcting a key source of errors, the researchers have demonstrated a promising approach for operating more qubits through shared microwave control lines.

According to recent reports, this is especially crucial for the development of large quantum processors. Giving every qubit its own independent control system would make increasingly complex devices difficult to manage. Shared control lines could offer a more practical way to expand these systems while maintaining the precision needed for quantum calculations.

Industry observers note that "By addressing a key source of control errors through pairwise calibration," states Camenzind. "Our study supports the use of shared control lines as a practical approach to scaling up quantum processors. Combined with silicon's compatibility with established semiconductor manufacturing, we believe that this advance could help pave the way toward larger quantum processors capable of performing increasingly complex computations.".

Industry observers note that the broader objective is to develop quantum computers that can reliably perform calculations despite the errors and disturbances that affect quantum systems. Such machines, known as fault-tolerant quantum computers, will require precise, dependable control over large numbers of qubits.

"Our long-term goal is to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer based on silicon spin qubits, and reliable parallel control is an essential step toward that goal," adds Seigo Tarucha, project manager of a silicon quantum computing project under JST's Moonshot Goal 6.

Materials provided by RIKEN. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, video game hardware manufacturers have been impacted by the computer component crisis, with Nintendo, PlayStation, and Xbox all raising the prices of their consoles this year. PC gaming giant Valve has increased the cost of its Steam Deck, and its PC-but-looks-like-a-console Steam Machine ended up being more expensive than Valve originally intended. Now, Valve has warned that its Steam Machine might get a price hike while opening up purchases for the cheapest model.

Recent findings suggest that in an patch posted on Thursday, Valve said it has fulfilled all reservations for the 512 GB Steam Machine model, which costs $1,049, and has now opened it up for purchase to anyone while supplies last. Nice! "However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts." Ah, nuts. Once the 512 GB model is sold out, Valve will mark it as out of stock instead of opening up a new waitlist.

According to Valve, there are more customers on the 2 TB model ($1,349) waitlist than its current production can meet. "Even when we are able to build more it will be at smaller quantities than we planned," Valve mentioned. There are more people on the 2 TB model waitlist than units made, so Valve is closing the waitlist. Those on the waitlist can purchase the 512 GB model, but they will be removed from the 2 TB model waitlist.

But here's the real kicker: Because PC parts continue to increase in price "at unprecedented levels," Valve is unsure how many Steam Machines it will be able to make, and unsure of how much they will be priced at when they're available. "The 2 TB model in particular will be especially constrained." Valve notes it will share more information in January.

For now, PC gamers contemplating purchasing a Steam Machine will have to wonder if they should pull the trigger now on the 512 GB model (especially before scalpers gobble them all up), take their chances on the 2 TB model waitlist, or hope for good news come January.

Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (647 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Space

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports.
  • It has been revealed that as stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby.
  • It has been revealed that "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in Fresh York, told Space.com.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports.

It has been revealed that as stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now.

It has been revealed that "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in Fresh York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect.".

In the fresh study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy. The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun.

According to recent reports, in 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018.

The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity.

Recent findings suggest that then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart.

"I was absolutely flabbergasted when we saw this," Karambelkar mentioned.

Industry observers note that in the latest study, the scientists estimated that the eruption expelled an amount of material equal to about 0.1 to 0.2 times the mass of the sun. "Stars engulfing their companions have been theorized for many decades, and this event provides the first observations of this theoretical prediction," Karambelkar mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that although these findings suggest that two stars — a binary system nicknamed "Bao" — merged into one, "it is not the only possibility," Karambelkar stated. "The other possibility is that both stars survived, in a much shorter orbit. In order to conclusively determine what happened, we need to continue monitoring what the system does, once the heft of the eruption settles down.".

Recent findings suggest that now that astronomers may have found the first such merger, "I can't wait to find more," Karambelkar mentioned. "Upcoming telescopes like the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Vera Rubin Observatory will be very useful in discovering many more such events.".

Recent findings suggest that the scientists detailed their findings Nov. 18 in the journal Nature.

According to recent reports, charles Q. Choi is a contributing writer for Space.com and Live Science. He covers all things human origins and astronomy as well as physics, animals and general science topics. However, with millions of gamers diving into Rockstar’s open world, several American police departments have issued warnings about copying the game’s criminal activities.

In a social media post shared ahead of launch, the Atlanta Police Department warned fans against bringing the chaos into the real world.

“GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!” the department wrote. “Don’t confuse virtual entertainment with real-life decisions.”.

It has been revealed that GTA is not a real place, but Atlanta is!🎮Don't confuse virtual entertainment with real-life decisions.Drunk driving, reckless driving, auto theft and violence have real consequences.Keep it in the game. Don't bring it to our streets. pic.twitter.com/Y7PdJFHLsZ.

The South Fulton Police Department issued a similar warning, reminding players that fictional crimes have no place on real streets.

Industry observers note that “Video games are fiction. Real crimes have real victims, and dangerous driving can change lives forever,” the department noted. “There’s no respawn, restart, or undo button.”.

The warnings haven’t been limited to Georgia.

As reported by the San Antonio Express-News, police departments in Texas have also been reminding players to keep their criminal activities confined to the game.

The San Juan Police Department published a GTA-inspired Instagram video featuring an officer closing a jail cell door alongside the franchise’s iconic “Busted” message.

Police can’t wait for GTA 6 to be released so they can “catch a break”.

Latest GTA 6 gameplay is so realistic fans can’t believe it’s not real life.

Police mock man for missing GTA 6 after dangerous car chase leads to arrest.

“We know you’re exciting and we know you’ve been waiting a long time, but what happens in GTA VI stays in GTA VI,” they mentioned.

Meanwhile, Floresville police warned that their city wasn’t an extension of Los Santos or Vice City and reminded players that officers aren’t NPCs.

They also warned that running red lights could result in a traffic stop, while changing a car’s color in an H-E-B parking lot wouldn’t make a real-world wanted level disappear.

Interestingly, these warnings come after the Greensboro Police Department in North Carolina said it couldn’t wait for GTA 6 to launch, hoping the game would keep people indoors and give officers a break.

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a upcoming generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity.
  • A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides latest insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them.
  • Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that tiny magnetic structures called skyrmions could help pave the way for a upcoming generation of computers that process information more like the human brain while using far less electricity. Although most people have never heard of skyrmions, these microscopic magnetic vortices may eventually play an important role in how computers store and process data.

A study published in the journal Nature Nanotechnology provides latest insights into how skyrmions behave and how scientists can control them. The findings could help researchers develop smaller, more efficient computing systems and advance emerging quantum technologies.

Most of the research was conducted at the Institute of Physics at Johannes Gutenberg University in Mainz, Germany, with contributions from a professor at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU).

"Skyrmions are small, magnetic vortices that can store information in a completely upcoming way," explained Asle Sudbø, who leads NTNU's Centre for Quantum Spintronics (QuSpin).

Unlike conventional technologies, which require increasing amounts of space and energy to handle growing quantities of data, skyrmions could offer a much more efficient alternative.

"Instead of the current technology, where we constantly need more space and energy to process data, skyrmions could make it possible to build much smaller and more energy-efficient data storage systems," explained Sudbø.

Tiny Magnetic Vortices Could Enable Brain-Like Computers.

Recent findings suggest that the potential applications of skyrmions extend well beyond conventional data storage. They are also vital to spintronics, which explores ways to use the magnetic properties of electrons in electronic devices, and to research involving topological quantum effects.

One particularly promising possibility is the development of computers that operate in ways similar to biological brains.

"These nanoscale vortices could help develop computers that resemble biological brains," said Sudbø.

Rather than relying on conventional transistor-based computing, such systems could use magnetism to process information. In principle, this approach could dramatically reduce electricity consumption, potentially allowing future computers to perform complex tasks with very little energy.

Turning that possibility into practical technology, however, requires scientists to understand exactly how skyrmions behave and how to manipulate them reliably.

The latest research represents an vital advance toward that goal.

Scientists Film Magnetic Skyrmion Lattices Melting for the First Time.

According to recent reports, skyrmions do not always exist as isolated magnetic structures. Under certain conditions, they organize themselves into repeating patterns known as lattices, resembling the orderly arrangement of atoms in a crystal, but on a much smaller scale.

Scientists can manipulate these arrangements, a capability that could be essential for using skyrmions in future computing devices.

Industry observers note that in the new study, researchers achieved something that had not been demonstrated before. They recorded the melting of a magnetic skyrmion lattice as it happened while simultaneously controlling individual skyrmions.

In a recent development, "For the first time, researchers have managed to film how a magnetic skyrmion lattice melts in real time, while simultaneously being able to manipulate each individual skyrmion directly as they film it. For example, both their shape and size can be changed 'on the fly'," said Sudbø.

The ability to observe this process directly provides a clearer picture of how skyrmions respond when their organized structures break apart. It also allows researchers to study how changing the size and shape of individual magnetic vortices affects their behavior.

A New Step Toward Energy-Efficient Computing.

Understanding how skyrmions behave during the breakdown of their lattices could help scientists develop more precise ways to control them. That control is particularly crucial if these magnetic structures are to become useful components in future computer systems.

The findings therefore offer more than a new way to observe an unusual magnetic phenomenon. They provide information that could help researchers overcome challenges involved in developing practical skyrmion-based technologies.

Industry observers note that "The findings give us latest insight into how these types of particles behave. This could therefore become notable for the development of more energy-efficient computer technology in the future," noted Sudbø.

Although substantial development is still needed before skyrmions can be used in everyday computing devices, the research highlights their potential for improving data storage, enabling upcoming computing architectures, and supporting advances in quantum technology.

By learning to observe and manipulate these tiny magnetic vortices in real time, scientists are gaining capabilities that could eventually help reshape the design of computers.

"This could revolutionize the way we think about computers," concluded Sudbø.

Breaking: Critical Java vulnerability puts millions of sites, services, and devices at risk of remote code execution

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (581 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomshardware

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the flaw was dubbed Java4Shell by Calif Research, the lab that found the vulnerability.
  • You can see an exploit of the bug in action below across multiple software services.
  • According to recent reports, the actual bug is a flaw in an optimization for Base64 decoding, functionality that's ubiquitous in any programming language.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the flaw was dubbed Java4Shell by Calif Research, the lab that found the vulnerability. The researchers say it rates 9.2 on the newer CVSS 4.0 scale, though individual reports from companies like Oracle itself and Red Hat give it their own ratings, but they're all in the 8 to 9.8 range depending on the vendor. The root cause is a bug in OpenJDK, the library that nearly every distribution of Java, whether Oracle's or anyone else's, derives their implementations from.

You can see an exploit of the bug in action below across multiple software services.

According to recent reports, the actual bug is a flaw in an optimization for Base64 decoding, functionality that's ubiquitous in any programming language. Base64 is a format to allow for easy transformation of binary data into plain text. In the modern day, it's used to embed files in the middle of text, like inserting image data in the middle of HTML or CSS, attaching files to emails (internally they're all text-based), or simply representing data as text for visual inspection, like file checksums or cryptographic key fingerprints.

Oracle has already fixed the bug and issued updated versions of its wares. However, much like digital certificates, operating systems and even individual programs include their own copy of a Java executable, meaning that the potential blast radius is far wider than you'd expect at first glance. Calif listed many such common applications: at the time of the post, Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, and PingFederate all had full unauthenticated RCE, while Apache Kafka Broker, Solr, Elasticsearch, Gerrit, and Spinnaker have RCEs after authentication.

In a recent development, because Java is so darn widespread, most every company has to issue security advisories and updates for their wares, including IBM, Red Hat, Siemens, and Broadcom. Because so many containers also use Java-based applications in some form, those too are vulnerable, and the count of individual vulnerable container images across registries everywhere is likely a high figure. This is likely not a bug that will be easily eradicated.

Sources indicate that there is a condition to trigger the exploit, but it's not too difficult to fulfill. The Java instance in question must be running on an x86-64 CPU with AVX-512 support and the VBMI extension. In practice, that means chips from the Intel Ice Lake and AMD Zen 4 families, from 2021 and 2022 respectively, for their server variants. Older CPUs are not affected, as the code optimization that contains the bug is specific to VBMI.

Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

The specific bug is in a hand-written assembly optimization that fails a simple bounds check. If an attacker inputs 64 As and an "=" sign as padding, they can overwrite neighboring memory, and then weaponize that corruption, similar to how Heartbleed worked. As usual these days, Calif indicates that the vulnerability was found by an AI bot, with $200 worth of tokens. Though unlike many other examples, this one was actually fairly deep, and it wasn't low-hanging fruit that illustrated poor code or network security hygiene.

Does GTA 6 have an 'easy mode'? Not officially, but there are two very important settings you can change to make the game less difficult

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story.
  • Sources indicate that but, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu.
  • Recent findings suggest that 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By now, you've probably heard that you cannot use cheats in GTA 6 until you complete the main story. Not only that, but enabling cheat codes also locks story progression and deactivates the ability to save. Basically, you can use cheats to have a quick crime spree and blow off some steam, then it's back to normalcy. Understandably, some gamers are a little put out with this change.

Sources indicate that but, for anyone looking to have a slightly easier time with GTA 6 than the dev's intended experience, I come with good news: you can make the game a little bit easier by toggling two options in the game's Settings menu. If you open Settings, and then navigate to Gameplay, you'll find 'Accessible Combat' and 'Reduced Vehicle Damage' toggles. You can activate both to make GTA 6's more difficult elements a little bit easier to work through.

Recent findings suggest that 'Accessible Combat' decreases enemy health and makes them deal less damage to your character — the kind of rebalancing that you'd expect from a traditional difficulty slider. 'Reduced Vehicle Damage', as you'd expect, lowers the damage taken by your vehicle and allows your ride to endure more punishment. This applies to gunfire, environmental threats, and impact damage.

Toggle these settings comes with a warning from Rockstar, though. A prompt notes that enabling these modifiers will "significantly change the balance and experience of the gameplay". I've been playing around with these settings and whilst they are not a foolproof 'God Mode' by any means, you can absolutely see a difference in the game when they're enabled: Jason and Lucia take a lot more punishment from melee damage and gunshots, and I had to really try to get Jason's old banged up pickup into even the 'slightly smoking' bracket of disrepair. Your mileage may vary, but these settings, from what I can tell so far, certainly do make the game easier.

Sources indicate that given that cheats disable trophies and progression, these settings might be something to keep in mind if you're trying to find a smoother path through the main story of GTA 6. It's a credit to Rockstar's accessibility teams that these have been included at all - alongside the 23 other gameplay accessibility options, the 12 display options, the 70 UI options, the 24 camera options, and the 14 audio options.

"We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," noted Rockstar's associate UI director, Sam Grosset, in materials provided to Eurogamer ahead of the game's launch. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone. We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like. Whether it's selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all.".

We also learned yesterday that Rockstar has made GTA 6 missions "harder to fail" by making them more open-ended, and giving players more ways to figure out how to do things in their own way.

If you need a hand with any of the myriad things GTA 6 asks you to do, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

  • Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.
  • OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

Also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

OpenAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

Industry observers note that if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The company already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

According to recent reports, gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

In a recent development, abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro strategy, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg mentioned Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent owners may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

In a recent development, AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

Also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

Sources indicate that the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US people can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

It has been revealed that the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The new landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

“Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

In a recent development, also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

In a recent development, “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release said. Google’s newly introduced Memory summary feature for Gemini lets users view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

Fiona, the beloved hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden, has died after accidentally swallowing a hat that became lodged in her habitat.

The zoo declared her death on November 19, revealing that its veterinary team had spent days attempting to save her after the incident occurred last week.

Despite multiple attempts to remove the hat from her system, Fiona’s condition became a medical emergency, and she ultimately did not recover.

In a statement shared on Instagram, the Cincinnati Zoo explained that Fiona had accidentally ingested a hat that ended up in her habitat last week.

“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo wrote.

According to the statement, veterinary staff made several attempts to remove the object, but were unable to do so successfully.

“The vet staff tried everything they could to help her after she ingested a hat that ended up in her habitat by accident last week. Despite multiple attempts to move the hat out of her system, it was ultimately too much to overcome.”.

A post shared by Cincinnati Zoo (@cincinnatizoo).

The zoo confirmed that Fiona received necessary supportive care on November 19 in a final attempt to save her life, but the treatment was unsuccessful.

Recent findings suggest that fiona became an international sensation after being born prematurely at the Cincinnati Zoo in January 2017. Weighing just 29 pounds at birth, she required round-the-clock care from zoo staff before eventually growing into one of the facility’s most recognizable animals.

Her early development was documented extensively on social media, attracting millions of followers and making her a prominent figure in the zoo’s conservation and educational efforts.

  • In a recent development, early in the game, Cal, a friend of co-protagonist Jason, spends an afternoon gaming with his buddy.
  • As GTA 6’s nearly 20 million players (at the time of this writing) know, GTA 6 is digital-only.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is now out everywhere, and players are discovering just how much this game is filled to the brim with an overwhelming amount of things to do. In the game’s opening hours, you’ll land a place on the water, steal a car from a police impound, get into a car chase, and more. There are a million little things to do, like playing video games inside GTA 6 itself.

In a recent development, early in the game, Cal, a friend of co-protagonist Jason, spends an afternoon gaming with his buddy. Ironically, he does something that IRL players can’t do with GTA 6 itself: bring a physical game disc with him.

As GTA 6’s nearly 20 million players (at the time of this writing) know, GTA 6 is digital-only. “Physical” copies simply contain a digital download code in a box. As such, you can’t bring your copy of GTA 6 to a friend’s house to show them the game like you could with previous GTA games, or like how Cal introduces Jason to Tenebrae Lux, a very artsy game that spoofs Jonathan Blow’s The Witness. (Jason’s not impressed; he’d rather go kill zombies.).

The two then have a party-filled night together that ends with them drunkenly fighting over who gets to sleep in the bed, which then cuts to the both of them sharing the bed in their undies. It’s a surprisingly wholesome sequence that includes Jason opening up about the strains in his relationship with Lucia on the eve of her getting released from prison. The moments of genuine friendship between Cal and Jason contrast well to the rest of GTA 6, which is all about, ya know, stealing drugs from rednecks, evading death-by-gator, running away from cops, and all other kinds of wild shenanigans.

Trading games, bringing a game disc to a hang sesh with the boys, introducing a upcoming game to a friend by popping your copy into their console — for years, sharing games was easy because they were all on discs or other physical formats. When I reviewed the Gears of War remaster last year (with a digital copy), it reminded me how I first played the original game by trading my copy of Assassin’s Creed with a friend for his copy of Gears. Fast-forward to this year, and I’m playing Pokémon Pokopia by borrowing my partner’s copy. (OK, maybe I stole it from her Switch 2 case, who can say.).

PlayStation once famously demonstrated how to share used games in a 2013 video intended as a dig toward the always-online Xbox One. That joke has aged like milk in the wake of Sony’s announcement that it will cease manufacturing physical discs for PlayStation games in January 2028. Sony’s news hit just a short time after Rockstar Games announced its own digital-only aims for GTA 6 back in June.

It has been revealed that sony’s move prompted a wave of angry commenters spamming every PlayStation promotional video and blog post with disdain ever since. Some PlayStation owners tried to wrangle together a “no disc, no buy” blackout campaign where they wouldn’t use PSN, make purchases at the PlayStation Store, or basically engage with their PlayStation console in any way. That blackout had no effect on Sony. In fact, Sony’s digital game sales have continued to grow since the announcement.

The outrage over the decline of physical games clearly hasn’t had an impact on Rockstar’s GTA 6 either. It broke preorder records, despite there being no real need to preorder a copy — they’re all digital, so Sony and Microsoft won’t be running out. This isn’t 2009, when you had to preorder a physical copy of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 to make sure you could pwn some newbz day one. (And snag a sleek poster in the process.).

Recent findings suggest that though we can’t say with certainty yet, it seems likely GTA 6 will end up as 2026’s top-selling game, in spite of the uproar around its lack of a disc version. Yet none of the eleventy billion people who buy it will be able to share it with their buds in the way that Cal shared a disc version of Tenebrae Lux with Jason.

#198. Breaking: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
